title: Bee
summary: A bee: a flying insect that feeds on nectar and pollen and pollinates flowers as it goes.

layers.basics: The bee flits between flowers. Its body is covered in branched hairs that catch pollen. Its big eyes are not like ours: each is made of thousands of tiny lenses packed side by side. Zoom in to see a simplified picture of that.
layers.deeper: Each of the two big eyes is a compound eye: a mosaic of many separate light-sensing units called ommatidia, each with its own lens. Together they give the bee a coarse image but very quick reaction to movement.
layers.expert: In an ommatidium a lens (cornea and crystalline cone) focuses light on a bundle of photoreceptor cells. The size and number of facets in the close-up are illustrative, not measured on a particular species.

facts: thousands of ommatidia per eye (the number depends on the species)
